theme: Comparative Indus urban construction histories and documentary activities
question: How do town designs, structures, materials, occupation sequences and local alterations compare, and which architectural relations can test the function of documentary objects?
outcome: 287 source-qualified assertions across twelve core towns and one hinterland relation; 42 source-use records, 38 checked paths representing 36 distinct held hashes; 134 quantity rows; complete 225-row local Dholavira seal-context extraction with scoped aggregates; six exploratory dimension-pair ratios; sixteen prior-output links and three untested conjectures. No fresh confirmation, new field measurement or global object-census gain.
challenge: Partial exposures, mixed building phases, historical date conventions, open chronological bounds, source conflicts and secondary deposits prevent whole-town counts or functional labels from raw site totals. An initial adapter failed and a second merge had semantic index and date-operator defects.
remedy: Preserve exact locators, raw quantities, phase namespaces, denominators and missing reasons; retain failed endpoints; review exact domain tags, unknown phases, open bounds and multi-site associations; separate architectural persistence from institutional mechanism and labour from generic provisioning; require independently coded primary contexts and a powered prospective comparison.
retry_when: New phase-keyed surveys, independent construction dates, physically identified primary-use documentary contexts and matched recovery denominators can discriminate common rules, supervision, engineering constraints and specific administrative functions. Do not rerun a town-level text correlation over the same examined corpus as fresh confirmation.

authors.model: GPT-6-family; exact serving variant not exposed
authors.role: coordinator and three research agents, with separate review and visual-production assignments
